must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: female passengers in Third Class had a drastically lower survival rate (24%) compared to females in First Class (96%)
must_find.reason: The report says gender is the strongest predictor (V=0.54) but never gives the overall female vs male rates (74% vs 19%) or states that women survived more.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: First Class:** 63.0% survival rate. *   **Second Class:** 47.3% survival rate. *   **Third Class:** 24.2% survival rate.
must_find.reason: Survival falls with class from first to third, with correct numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Survivors paid an average fare of **$48.40**, whereas non-survivors paid an average of **$22.12**.
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares on average, stated with numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: Missingness is heavily skewed toward Third Class (479 cases) and Southampton embarkation (515 cases)
must_find.reason: The report discusses cabin missingness but never says that passengers without a cabin survived less often.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: when Cabin is missing, the probability of Age being missing jumps from ~9% to ~23%.
must_find.reason: It relates Age missingness to Cabin missingness but not to survival.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: Model training was interrupted due to a missing import statement for `LogisticRegression`.
must_find.reason: No model was fit or compared with a baseline.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: The report states that no precision/recall results exist.

must_not_claim.quote: The dataset contains 342 survivors (38.4%) and 549 non-survivors.
must_not_claim.reason: The report correctly says most passengers did not survive.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.reason: The report never claims men survived more than women.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: Passengers in First Class had a 63% survival rate compared to only 24% for Third Class
must_not_claim.reason: It states first class survived more, the opposite of the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: Survival probability was primarily a function of **Socioeconomic Status (Class)**, followed closely by **Gender**, and then **Age**.
must_not_claim.reason: The report ranks Age third, not as the strongest predictor.

caveats.quote: **Data Quality Issues:** 77% of 'Cabin' data is missing, limiting the utility of specific cabin locations without imputation or binning.
caveats.reason: The report explicitly lists missing Cabin data as a limitation.
